articles.title: “They've been there with me every step along”: How Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf surprise Las Vegas charity with $1 million donation after years of support
articles.summary: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf made an unexpected announcement at a Las Vegas charity gala in April 2017.
articles.body: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf made an unexpected announcement at a Las Vegas charity gala in April 2017. The tennis legends pledged $1 million to Keep Memory Alive, a nonprofit that supports the Cleveland Clinic Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health. The donation came during an evening when Agassi received an award for his charitable work. But before making the announcement, he took a moment to thank two people who had stood behind him throughout his journey off the court.Andre Agassi makes surprise $1 million announcement at Las Vegas galaThe moment came on April 27, 2017, at the 21st annual Power of Love gala at the MGM Grand Garden Arena. Agassi received the Community Leadership Award at the event, which raises money for the Cleveland Clinic Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health.During his speech, the former tennis champion spoke about the support he had received from centre founder Larry Ruvo and his wife, Camille. He credited the couple for helping him with his charitable work in education."They've been there with me every step along the way, sometimes next to me, sometimes behind me, pushing me a little bit. Quite often I've found them under me, giving me their shoulders to stand on, and I can't thank you enough for that," Agassi said during his acceptance speech at the gala.Then came the surprise. Agassi announced that he and his wife, Steffi Graf, would donate $1 million to Keep Memory Alive. The pledge drew loud applause from the audience. Even Ruvo had not expected the announcement."He went way off script," Ruvo said after Agassi revealed the donation, according to the Las Vegas Review-Journal's. Ruvo embraced Agassi and thanked the couple. He also called the former tennis champion a hometown hero. What began as an award presentation had turned into another major contribution to the organisation. Their previous $1.5 million gift helped support brain health researchThe million-dollar pledge was not their first contribution to the centre. In January 2015, Agassi and Graf had donated $1.5 million directly to the Cleveland Clinic Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health.The Associated Press reported the donation on January 11, 2015. Larry Ruvo praised the couple's generosity, describing it as "an extraordinary gift by a very wonderful man."He told the Las Vegas Sun that the money would help the centre expand its research work for the community.The facility provides treatment for people living with Alzheimer's, Huntington's and Parkinson's diseases. It also cares for patients with frontotemporal dementia and multiple sclerosis.There is another important distinction between the two contributions. The 2015 donation went directly to the brain health centre, while the 2017 pledge went to Keep Memory Alive, the nonprofit organisation that exclusively supports the facility.Agassi's words at the 2017 gala offered a glimpse into the personal connection behind the donations. He did not simply accept an award and leave the stage. He used the occasion to recognise the people who had supported his charitable efforts and announced a contribution alongside Graf. articles.title: Jean Fernandes responde a los rumores de su salida del América de Cali
articles.standfirst: ¿Se va de los 'Escarlatas'? La tajante reacción de Jean Fernandes sobre su futuro en el América
articles.summary: ¿Se va de los 'Escarlatas'? La tajante reacción de Jean Fernandes sobre su futuro en el América
articles.body: El futuro del arco escarlata se convirtió en el tema más caliente del rentado nacional. Tras los fuertes rumores desde el exterior que sitúan al guardameta brasileño Jean Fernandes en la Liga MX de México para la temporada 2027, el propio jugador y el cuerpo técnico del América de Cali se pronunciaron al respecto. En las últimas horas, periodistas especializados en fichajes a nivel internacional aseguraron que el portero brasileño tendría todo acordado para marcharse a condición de agente libre rumbo al Necaxa de México, firmando un contrato por tres años con opción a uno más. La noticia generó conmoción absoluta entre la hinchada del cuadro americano, especialmente por el rendimiento superlativo que ha mostrado el guardameta, consolidándose como una de las piezas inamovibles del esquema de David González. Ante el revuelo mediático, Jean Fernandes usó sus redes sociales para manifestarse con ironía y dejar en claro su postura ante las especulaciones de la prensa: “La gente sabe más de mi vida que yo mismo”, expresó el guardameta brasileño en sus plataformas digitales, desatando todo tipo de comentarios entre los aficionados. Asimismo, el arquero ha señalado en repetidas oportunidades su comodidad en la capital del Valle del Cauca, su deseo de conquistar títulos con la camiseta de los 'Diablos Rojos' y la felicidad de su familia en el país, recordando que su vínculo contractual con la institución rige hasta el próximo 31 de diciembre. Por su parte, el estratega David González sorprendió en plena rueda de prensa tras ser interrogado por el supuesto traspaso al fútbol mexicano, admitiendo que no tenía conocimiento de la situación: "Me entero por lo que me estás diciendo tú. No tengo conocimiento", afirmó de manera tajante el timonel antioqueño, dejando en evidencia que, al interior del club, el enfoque actual pasa estrictamente por los cuadrangulares de la Liga BetPlay. Con un contrato próximo a expirar y sin una propuesta formal de renovación sobre la mesa por parte de la directiva escarlata —según ha deslizado su entorno cercano—, el futuro de Jean Fernandes sigue siendo una incógnita gigante. Mientras la afición espera que la directiva acelere las gestiones para asegurar su continuidad de cara al año de su centenerio, el portero continúa concentrado en cerrar de la mejor manera el semestre actual y guiar al América hacia la estrella.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on CM Punk, Shawn Michaels, AJ Styles, Gunther vs. Balor, Crown Jewel Match Change
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

WWE's Reported Plans for NXT Amid Administrative Shake-Up

With WWE Hall of Famer Shawn Michaels potentially moving into a bigger role within WWE, several big names reportedly may be in line to pick up the slack in NXT.

According to Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t Steve Carrier Ringside News), the "most likely scenario" will see WWE Hall of Famer AJ Styles replace Michaels as the head of NXT.

Alvarez added that current WWE Superstars CM Punk and Bayley may have input and roles in NXT as well.

On Thursday, PWInsider.com's Mike Johnson reported that WWE is planning to promote Michaels from NXT head to executive director of creative writing and talent as the replacement for Bruce Prichard.

Per Johnson, Prichard is expected to transition into a different role that will allow him to work from home rather than being on location in Stamford, Connecticut.

However, Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t Wrestle Features ) reported Friday that the plan is for Bobby Roode and Ed Koskey to split the duties being vacated by Prichard.

Meltzer noted that Prichard's job includes "administrative work," which Michaels has never done before, plus he is considered a valuable commodity in NXT.

Nothing is certain yet, though, as Meltzer added that things could change multiple times between now and when the final decision has to be made in April.

If Michaels does move into Prichard's position and leave NXT behind, the developmental brand still figures to be in great hands since Styles, Punk and Bayley are among the all-time greats and widely regarded for their ability to work with younger talent.

Gunther vs. Balor Reportedly in Question for Crown Jewel

There is reportedly some uncertainty regarding whether Gunther and Finn Balor will clash at Crown Jewel next weekend.

According to Meltzer (h/t WrestlePurists ), Gunther vs. Balor was originally planned for Crown Jewel, and if it is no longer happening, then it is a case of the card being changed and those working on the venue in Saudi Arabia not being aware of it.

Meltzer was referencing the fact that advertising was spotted this week in Saudi Arabia for a Gunther vs. Balor match at Crown Jewel:

WWE has yet to officially announce that match, although it could potentially happen during Friday night's episode of SmackDown.

Gunther and Balor have been at odds on SmackDown for several weeks due to their common goal of trying to win the WWE Championship.

They have gotten into some scuffles, but it hasn't led to a match yet, as Gunther has been preoccupied with Danhausen.

Balor already saved Danhausen from an attack at the hands of Gunther once, and if he steps in again this week on SmackDown, that could be the impetus behind a match at Crown Jewel.

Reported Original Plans for The Vision vs. Penta and Evans

Penta and Je'Von Evans reportedly weren't originally slated to challenge The Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory for the World Tag Team Championships at Crown Jewel.

According to Meltzer (h/t WrestlePurists ), the initial plan for Crown Jewel was a six-man tag team match pitting Penta, Evans and Oba Femi against Breakker, Theory and Bronson Reed.

However, it was ultimately decided that it wouldn't make sense to do the six-man tag before giving Penta and Evans a title shot.

Penta and Evans beat Breakker and Theory in a non-title match a few weeks ago, and they have continued to be at odds with The Vision ever since then.

Following Evans losing his WWE Championship match against Sami Zayn this week on Raw, The Vision attacked Je'Von. Penta attempted to make the save, but he was beaten down instead.

Penta and Evans then appealed to Raw general manager Adam Pearce for a tag team title opportunity, and it was granted.

Although Femi and Reed won't officially be part of the title match at Crown Jewel, it is easy to envision both of them getting involved.

articles.title: El número 1, al rojo vivo en la final de Kuwait
articles.standfirst: Triay y Brea volvieron a una final 55 días después venciendo a Claudia y Martina
articles.summary: Triay y Brea volvieron a una final 55 días después venciendo a Claudia y Martina
articles.body: Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero volvieron a demostrar que nunca se rinden. Las catalanas remontaron ante Bea González y Paula Josemaría (4-6, 7-6 y 7-6) en una semifinal de máxima exigencia que se prolongó durante tres horas y 43 minutos. Una victoria de enorme mérito que les permite alcanzar su tercera final de Major en tres torneos disputados esta temporada, afianzar la segunda posición de la Race y seguir presionando por el número uno. Bea y Paula comenzaron mejor, imponiendo su ritmo y encontrando en Josemaría a su principal referencia ofensiva. Con un juego muy sólido, se escaparon hasta el 5-2 y terminaron cerrando el primer set por 6-4. El guion parecía repetirse en la segunda manga, cuando volvieron a tomar una ventaja de 3-0. Sin embargo, Ari y Andrea reaccionaron, elevaron su nivel y consiguieron llevar el parcial al tie-break, donde terminaron forzando el tercer set. La última manga fue una auténtica batalla. Bea y Paula volvieron a tener el partido en sus manos, llegando incluso a disponer del saque para colocarse 5-2. Pero las catalanas resistieron una vez más, recuperaron el terreno perdido y llevaron la semifinal a un nuevo desempate. Aunque sus rivales consiguieron igualar el 4-1 inicial, Ari y Andrea encontraron la manera de cerrar el encuentro y completar una remontada que vuelve a confirmar su enorme capacidad competitiva. En la otra semifinal, Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea tuvieron que trabajar mucho para superar a Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo. Las número uno se llevaron el primer set por 6-4, pero las jóvenes españolas reaccionaron con un segundo parcial sobresaliente, que dominaron por 6-2. Todo quedó pendiente de una tercera manga muy igualada, resuelta finalmente en el tie-break a favor de Gemma y Delfi, que sellaron su victoria por 6-4, 2-6 y 7-6. De esta manera, las número uno regresan a una final 55 días después y tendrán enfrente a sus principales perseguidoras. Con el cara a cara igualado a seis victorias, Kuwait decidirá un nuevo capítulo de una rivalidad que también tiene en juego el liderato de la Race. Ari y Andrea llegan lanzadas, con tres finales de Major en tres oportunidades y la posibilidad de dar otro golpe sobre la mesa.

articles.title: Para-cycling Track World Championships: Kadeena Cox sets new world record to win gold
articles.summary: Great Britain's Kadeena Cox sets a new world record as she wins C4 1km gold at the Para-cycling Track World Championships in the Netherlands.
articles.body:
Great Britain's Kadeena Cox set a new world record as she won C4 1km gold at the Para Cycling Track World Championships in the Netherlands.

The 35-year-old crossed the line in 1 minute 9.545 seconds to win her seventh world title.

Cox faced a nervous wait as Tara Neyland took to the track afterwards in pursuit of a medal, but her Australian rival could not eclipse the Briton's time.

Cox, who is a five-time Paralympic gold medallist, was draped in a British flag by her team following victory as she joyously celebrated her first world title since 2024.

In the men's tandem B 1km time-trial, Britain's James Ball defended his title as he won gold alongside new partner Aaron Pope.

The pair dominated in the final, crossing the line in 59.563 seconds as Ball secured his eighth world title, with Pope winning his first.

In the women's pursuit final, Britain's Sophie Unwin alongside Jenny Holl won silver behind New Zealand's gold medallists Emma Foy and Jessie Hodges.

Unwin and Holl had earlier set a new world record of 4:30.262 in qualifying, before it was broken by Foy and Hodges' time of 4:29.672.

In the men's C4 final, Britain's Archie Atkinson won bronze, while compatriot Fin Graham also took bronze in the C3 1km time-trial.

articles.title: Why an Emilio Pagán decision is key to Cincinnati Reds' playoff future
articles.summary: Cincinnati closer Emilio Pagán (19-for-19 in save chances, 1.88 ERA after a hamstring injury) is one of 3 Reds with contract decisions due Oct. 31.
articles.body:
It doesn't take a baseball genius to identify the first, biggest order of business for the Cincinnati Reds after watching this year's World Series.

The division-rival Brewers rode one of the best bullpen runs in postseason history to stream-roll the field — including a sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers along the way.

Their collective 1.38 ERA over 65 postseason innings ranked second in history (minimum 50 innings) to the 2022 Astros. And to put it in 2026 context, only one reliever in baseball this year had an ERA that low in at least 50 innings.

Which meant on average, the Brewers sent All-Star Blue Jays closer Louis Varland to the mound every time they made a pitching change this October.

So how important is Pagán – one of the best closers in the game the past two seasons – to the Reds in their very public quest to try to return to the playoffs under manager Terry Francona in 2027?

Pagán, 35, is one of three Reds with an Oct. 31 option deadline in play for his 2027 status with the club, the only one with a better-than-slim chance to return. His is a player option for $10 million, coming off a season in which he missed two months with a hamstring injury – and then was dominant the rest of the way.

The two others are DH Eugenio Suárez and reliever Pierce Johnson, neither one of which is expected to have his mutual option exercised by the club.

Pagán leaned on the counsel of his longtime agent as he took the decision into the final hours before the deadline, at least the business part of the decision.

"I haven't been shy. Everybody here knows this. I like it here," said Pagán, who has been with the Reds since signing the first of a pair of two-year free-agent deals before the 2024 season. "I want to be a part of the solution to get this organization going where it needs to be. That's where my mindset is."

The Reds made the playoffs in 2025 on the final day of the season, about five months after Pagán took over the closer role full-time, before converting a career-high 32 saves with a 2.88 ERA. He suffered one of the lengthier injuries for a pitching staff crushed by health issues, before returning to convert all 19 save chances with a 1.88 ERA.

His influence as a veteran on younger pitchers on the staff has been almost as impressive.

Pagán didn't expect to jump into the free agent market as he spoke near the end of the season. But he also needed to weigh the business realities of his contract option, whether that means wading into a free agent market fraught with a looming labor lockout or seeking the chance to add more length to the Reds deal.

"I'm not worried about any kind of a business decision," he said. "I anticipate being on this team and hopefully trying to not just get back into the playoffs next year but compete for a division championship. Obviously, we've proven we've got a pretty serious way to go. So I'd love to be a part of that solution."

That uphill climb only looks more serious, and daunting, after watching the Brewers do to every challenger in October what they've done to the Reds in almost every series the last five years.

If nothing else, Milwaukee's recipe for success underscored the Reds' plan. If they're healthy, they start with a competitive starting rotation.

As for the lineup, offensively and defensively, the front office has an implausible task to shore things up this winter.

But when it comes to the bullpen, the return of Pagán could be a significant start to at least being able to dream a little about turning that 75-87 debacle of a 2026 season into something that approaches at least the fringes of the wild-card race by September.

"It's a good feeling to feel like I'm doing my job and coming through for my team," he said of his post-injury performance. "But being in the playoffs is more important than individual statistics. So it's unfortunate this season didn't go the way we wanted it to. I'm glad I'm coming through and doing my job, but I wish it was for more meaningful games."

articles.title: Fantasy Football Injury Update: Great News for Jeremiyah Love and Michael Wilson Managers; Both Active for Week 8
articles.summary: Great news for fantasy managers as Jeremiyah Love and Michael Wilson clear the injury report and suit up for Week 8. Get the breakdown on their expected role...
articles.body:
Fantasy managers with any equity in the Arizona Cardinals who are navigating the grueling midway point of the NFL season just caught a massive break. Ahead of a critical Week 8 slate, two key offensive contributors have avoided game-day designations as RBJeremiyah Love and WR Michael Wilson have both been officially declared good to go.

Getting both of these impact players back on the field is exceptionally welcome news for fantasy managers who have been scrambling to patch together starting lineups amid a wave of recent injuries and bye-week crunches. Let's take a look at the fantasy football ripple effects for Week 8.

Starting in the backfield, the return of Jeremiyah Love is a major boost, though managers should maintain a sense of cautious optimism as he shakes off the rust from his recent ankle ailment. Love immediately slots back into the RB2 range in our Week 8 Running Back Rankings . Given his explosive ceiling, high-value touches and a dream Week 8 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, he makes an absolute must-start. Dallas has struggled immensely to contain ground attacks, coughing up 22.6 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing running backs (ranking them as a bottom-tier, Top 8-most-friendly matchup for the position).

Even if Love sees a slightly managed snap share in his first game back, his explosive big-play ability matches up wonderfully against a defense leaking chunk yardage on the ground. Unfortunately, this clean bill of health comes with a downside for fantasy opportunists: temporary fill-ins like Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier are officially downgraded back to the waiver wire . With Love reclaiming his workload, those substitute options lose their standalone fantasy viability and can safely be dropped if you need to churn your bench for upside.

Meanwhile, Arizona wideout Michael Wilson is also fully cleared for action despite managing a rib issue earlier in the week. While Wilson hasn't quite put up staggering fantasy numbers over his last few outings, his outlook has drastically shifted upward following the blockbuster trade that sent Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston. As the clear focal point of this passing attack, Wilson steps into a funnel-like target share and lands comfortably as a reliable WR2 or high-end Flex option in our Week 8 Wide Receiver Rankings .

That projection gets an even bigger boost squaring off against a porous Dallas secondary that surrenders 29.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wide receivers (ranking them among the bottom-6 units in generosity to wideouts). This matchup ensures Wilson will see ample opportunity to exploit soft coverage holes all afternoon. This update also represents a stability upgrade for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, while filtering down to mean fewer manufactured targets for secondary wideouts like Kendrick Bourne. As for superstar tight end Trey McBride, managers shouldn't fret too much about target cannibalization; elite tight ends of his caliber remain locked-in every-week studs regardless of how the outside receiver targets shake out.

articles.title: Red Roses cruise to dominant victory over United States in final WXV game
articles.summary: English rugby chiefs have been on a charm offensive in the United States this week, but the players on the pitch opted for more of a brute-force approach.
articles.body:
English rugby chiefs have been on a charm offensive in the United States this week, but the players on the pitch opted for more of a brute-force approach.

The Red Roses were in the unfamiliar position of coming off the back of successive defeats and Meg Jones had called on her team to respond. They certainly did that, looking far more like world champions than they have over the past fortnight with a convincing nine - try win – four of them scored by Claudia Moloney-MacDonald – albeit there is still room for them to "grow", as Jones put it after the game.

That is what the Rugby Football Union have been trying to do off the field. Bill Sweeney, the RFU chief executive, and his colleagues used this fixture in New Jersey as an opportunity to tap into the US market by "creating connections" with business leaders and potential investors.

It is little wonder English rugby is trying to get a piece of the American pie. There are an ever-growing number of US owners in British football and with the States hosting the men's and women's Rugby World Cups in 2031 and 2033 interest in the oval-ball game is sure to grow too, although the crowd in New Jersey would suggest there is work to do on that front.

Those potential investors at the Sports Illustrated Stadium may not have enjoyed seeing their national team so convincingly beaten, but they will surely have recognised the talent of those wearing white.

England fell short of the high standards they are known for in those defeats by Canada – their first back-to-back losses in a decade – but there were marked improvements against the US. Yes, there were still a few defensive frailties and they will be disappointed by their ill-discipline at times, but their attacking play looked far slicker.

In part, that was because the US did not close down the Red Roses as effectively as their Canadian counterparts, but the visitors' handling was far sharper than it has been on this away leg of the WXV Global Series.

Holly Aitchison, who replaced Zoe Harrison at fly-half in one of six changes made by John Mitchell for this Test, showed what a classy distributor she is. First came a floated pass out to Moloney-MacDonald to dive over for the opening try inside five minutes. Then, as England switched the attack from right to left, there was a pinpoint long pass to the same winger to run in her second.

There were deft hands, too, for England's third try as the backs ran a set play from a line-out in the 22: Emma Sing, popping the ball to captain Meg Jones to score the easiest of tries.

The forwards got in on the act as well. Mackenzie Carson releasing Maud Muir for a stand-out run at the start of the second half that led to Moloney-MacDonald's third try and she quickly scored her fourth after another long pass from Jones.

Moloney-MacDonald was dropped after the first defeat by Canada in Toronto having dropped the ball over the line in the opening minutes but she made amends here.

The US had come into this match on the back of five straight wins and they did have a few stand-out moments. Alev Kelter was uncompromising in her tackles – she seemed to be on a personal mission to beast Jones – and Hope Rogers' first-half try epitomised the grit of their forwards.

But they still lack the all-court game to compete with the Red Roses, who wrapped up this victory with four tries in the last quarter from Mia Venner, Bryony Field (on her 26th birthday), Maddie Feaunati and Sadia Kabeya.

The Red Roses have shown what investment can deliver on the pitch; the RFU will now be hoping this performance will bring some US dollars into the English game.

That is the final act of the game and England close out a 55-12 victory in New Jersey. Is that the start of another long winning streak for the Red Roses? That is the final game for England in 2026, with their next game coming away against Wales in the Six Nations in April.

The hosts finish the game with their second try of the night. Their rolling maul, with nearly every player involved, nearly got to the line but a few phases later they do get across the whitewash through Zackary. The conversion is missed.

As we tick into the final minute, England are penalised just outside their 22, allowing the US to kick towards the corner for one final chance of a try.

The US are back up to 15 as Tupou returns from her time in the bin.

The Red Roses were denied going past 50 points moments ago but this time they will not be. Jones and Venner were both brought down just shy of the try line but Kabeya powers over from close range. Harrison adds the extras.

England thought they had gone past the 50-point mark with a fine try from Bern but the try is disallowed as the pass to Bern from Botterman is adjudged to have been forward. Bern will be gutted as that was a fine finish from the prop.

Not a massive surprise to see England opt for the scrum.

That is a hugely dominant scrum from England, who have two new props on the field. That earns England the penalty as the US pack was marched backwards.

As well as bringing Kildunne on, England have also introduced Harrison.

Kildunne is on for England, which draws big cheers from the crowd in New Jersey.

She has had to see Moloney-MacDonald go over for four tries tonight and finally Venner gets on the scoresheet as the ball is shipped from left to right and good handling all the way down the line sees Venner go over in the corner. England make a switch at scrum-half as Hunt comes on for Robinson, yet another example of the quality on England's bench tonight.

USA are very likely to lose this game but they have got pumped about that moment. Kelter absolutely smashes Jones back in a huge tackle before USA steal possession. That gets the US players and fans fired up. That was probably the loudest ths stadium has been all night.

England are now dipping into their immense resources on the bench with a double prop change as Botterman and Bern enter the fray.

Jones whips a long pass out to the left wing, where Moloney-MacDonald has the easiest of finishes for her fourth try. Moloney-MacDonald would probably want to play every week in New Jersey. England have a scrum just outside the US 22 and their pack then dominates again at scrum time to win the penalty, which they put into the corner.

England then earn themselves a penalty advantage at the lineout. Eventually, we come back for the original penalty.

England win the first penalty of the half, just inside the US half, and opt to take it quickly.

It is safe to say that John Mitchell has plenty of ammunition on his bench, including the likes of Hannah Botterman, Ellie Kildunne, Zoe Harrison and Natasha Hunt. In fact, it is a pretty formidable bench and I would guess that England will dip into their bench fairly quickly into the second half.

Five reasons why Red Roses have become beatable

While England did well to absorb large amounts of red zone pressure in the first half, it ultimately knackered them. This was particularly pronounced when Canada seamlessly spread the ball to the edges or caught England out with their sparky transition play, calling the Red Roses' backs into action. It was perfectly encapsulated by the hosts' second try, when Lucy Packer, Helena Rowland and Mia Venner all gave chase to Gabby Senft in the build up to Sophie de Goede's score. None of them laid a glove on either forward. The problems compounded in the second half when Flo Symonds's scything run through Emma Sing and Jess Breach was the attacking platform for de Goede's second, before Savannah Bauder bumped off Sing for Canada's fifth and final try. England Women's WXV campaign comes to an end in New Jersey as they take on the United States in the Red Roses' final game of 2026. A matter of weeks ago, England were still on their incredible winning streak, which was ended by a draw on home soil against Canada. Since then, the Red Roses have suffered their second straight defeat against Canada, which means that John Mitchell's side have now lost back-to-back games for the first time in 10 years. England have won just two of their five WXV games during this campaign, which includes two defeats and a draw.

"Our intent is to start this next phase strongly against the USA, with six months until our next Test in the Guinness Women's Six Nations," Mitchell said. "We are rotating some positions this week to refresh the group, create opportunities and continue building our depth. Selection is driven by what the team needs against the USA, the behaviours we value and the performance we are preparing to deliver. Everyone has a role, and everyone is accountable for our standards."

Mitchell has made six changes to his starting XV, with Flo Robinson making her first international start at scrum-half. England duo Zoe Harrison and Megan Jones are among four nominees for World Rugby Women's 15s Player of the Year award. The winner of that award will be announced following this weekend's final WXV Global Series matches.

The United States have won back-to-back home games against Italy this month to build up to this final game of the campaign. That followed up wins over Ireland and Wales in September.

"I do not think they [England] are going to try new things," USA head coach Jack Hanratty said. "I think they are going to put out an incredibly strong team to try and not only show the world that they are, if not number one, they still want to show that they are number one. And to do that would be not only winning a game, but showing dominance in everything. Our job this week is to challenge them. We want to see what aspects of the game have we grown that we can challenge the world's best? That is our job. I think we have got a bit of an opportunity for a free hit. But I love the fact that we are coming into it with momentum. It is at the end of an eight-week tour, and it is amazing that our meetings are still energetic and our training sessions are still actually of quality."

Kick-off from New Jersey is at 9.15pm GMT.

articles.title: Commanders DT Daron Payne ruled out vs. Eagles with serious foot injury
articles.summary: Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne suffered a significant foot injury and has been ruled out against the Eagles, further weakening Washington's defensiv...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles will face a significantly depleted Washington Commanders defensive line Sunday night after standout defensive tackle Daron Payne suffered a serious foot injury during Friday's practice. According to NFL Network insiders Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo, Payne sustained an injury expected to sideline him for the foreseeable future and could lead to a stint on injured reserve.

Washington initially listed the veteran defensive tackle as questionable after he was limited during Friday's practice, but the Commanders subsequently downgraded him to out for Sunday's NFC East matchup.

Payne is scheduled to undergo additional evaluations Saturday to determine the injury's severity and how much time he could miss.

The development is another significant setback for Washington, which has already ruled out defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw with a knee injury. Kinlaw did not practice Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday, leaving the Commanders without two important interior defenders against Philadelphia. Hogs Haven+1

Eagles could exploit Washington's depleted interior

Payne's absence creates a potentially favorable matchup for an Eagles offensive line attempting to establish consistency after Monday night's 38-21 loss to Dallas.

Philadelphia has dealt with significant running back injuries, but Saquon Barkley returned to practice Friday after missing the previous two sessions with hamstring and back injuries. The former All-Pro received no final game-status designation, putting him on track to face Washington.

Barkley's expected availability becomes even more important with the Commanders missing Payne and Kinlaw.

Philadelphia could look to attack the interior of Washington's defensive front behind guards Landon Dickerson and Tyler Steen and center Drew Kendall.

The Eagles have struggled to establish their rushing attack during a five-game losing streak. Still, Washington's injuries could give offensive coordinator Sean Mannion opportunities to lean on Barkley early and ease pressure on quarterback Tanner McKee.

Washington faces difficult defensive line decisions.

With Payne and Kinlaw out, the Commanders may have to rely more on their remaining defensive tackles and adjust their rotation. Second-year defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton was listed as questionable with a pectoral injury after practicing on a limited basis throughout the week. Newton is also working through the process of returning from injured reserve, meaning Washington must address his roster status before he can play.

The uncertainty leaves the Commanders facing tough personnel decisions against an Eagles offense that has been effective in the red zone.

Philadelphia enters Week 8 ranked fourth in red-zone touchdown efficiency at 73.7%, while Washington ranks last in red-zone defense, allowing touchdowns on 81.8% of opponents' opportunities.

The Eagles have struggled to move the ball consistently, but Barkley's potential return, combined with Washington's injuries, could create an opportunity to improve their offense. Philadelphia enters Sunday's matchup at 2-5, looking to end a five-game losing streak. Washington is 1-4-1 and attempting to avoid another NFC East defeat.

Payne's injury could have consequences well beyond Sunday's gam. Still, his absence immediately changes the trench matchup and gives the Eagles a chance to establish the physical running game they have lacked in recent weeks.

articles.title: Deeper Than Hate Rivalry On Halloween
articles.summary: App State and Georgia Southern clash Saturday in Statesboro. See the stats, the history, and why this Sun Belt East game matters more than most.
articles.body:
Two Sun Belt East rivals meet in Statesboro on a Saturday that doubles as Halloween . App State travels to Paulson Stadium for a 6:30 p.m. ET kickoff against Georgia Southern. This matchup matters more than a typical conference game because it decides who stays alive in the division race. Both teams need a win to keep their hopes for a title shot alive. The series carries a nickname that fans take seriously: "Deeper Than Hate." That phrase was born from decades of hard hits and close scores, not just marketing fluff.

History shows a tight split in the all-time record. App State leads the series 21-19-1 after 41 meetings, but the recent trend favors the Eagles. Georgia Southern has won the last three games and four of the last five contests. The most recent meeting ended on Dec. 29, 2025, in the Birmingham Bowl, where Georgia Southern crushed App State 29-10. That neutral-site game marked the first time the two programs met in a bowl since moving to FBS. OJ Arnold ran for 152 yards in that bowl win, proving the Eagles could dominate when it counted most.

App State enters this game with a 5-2 record and a 2-1 mark in the Sun Belt. The Mountaineers rode a high after beating previously unbeaten James Madison 34-31 in overtime on Oct. 22. James London kicked a 40-yard field goal to seal that win in front of a sold-out crowd in Boone. That victory put every team in the East Division at risk of losing the lead. Georgia Southern sits at 3-4 overall but holds a 2-1 record in conference play. Their win over Old Dominion on Oct. 15 snapped a four-game losing streak that looked ugly for a long time.

The Eagles have played the exact same three league foes as App State this season. They beat Coastal Carolina 31-24 and Old Dominion 23-15 but lost at home to JMU 27-24. Their nonconference losses came against strong teams like Clemson and No. 18 Houston. Those tough losses mean their 3-4 record is misleading compared to their actual talent level. Per App State Athletics , the team is ready for a difficult challenge after avenging earlier losses to Coastal Carolina and JMU. The midweek victory against ODU was their last game, giving them 16 days to rest before this showdown.

Both squads deal with injury questions at the most important spot on the field. Georgia Southern quarterback Max Johnson is listed as probable to play after leaving the ODU game with a first-half injury. This season, the left-handed offspring of ex-NFL quarterback Brad Johnson has tallied 11 touchdowns. Johnson averages 262.0 yards through the air in his first six starts. If he cannot go, Turner Helton or Weston Bryan will step in as running threats from the backfield. Bryan is the second-leading rusher for an offense that has struggled with depth at running back.

App State quarterback Malachi Singleton started against JMU after missing the second half of the Coastal Carolina game. In that overtime victory, he finished 26 of 40 passes for 271 yards while scoring two touchdowns. The Mountaineers played shorthanded due to injuries at key spots, including left tackle. This week's availability report lists Devon Manuel as out for the season. On defense, team captain Colton Phares led the way with 13 tackles against the Dukes. Last week, a PFN grade of 99.0 placed him first among FBS linebackers. That defensive effort was the reason App State held JMU to just 92 rushing yards.

This game is a battle for the Sun Belt East title. A loss for either team could effectively end their season. The rivalry started in 1932 when South Georgia Teachers beat App State 33-0 in Statesboro. It gained modern status in the 1987 I-AA quarterfinals when App State shut out the Eagles 19-0. The 2022 game was the highest-scoring meeting ever, with Georgia Southern winning 51-48 in double overtime. Three other overtime games have happened between these two, showing how evenly matched they usually are.

Clay Helton is in his fifth season as head coach for Georgia Southern. Dowell Loggains is in his second season leading the Mountaineers in Boone. The winner of this Halloween night clash will likely control their own destiny for the rest of the year. Fans know this series goes back to the days of FCS national titles for both programs. Both teams moved to the FBS and the Sun Belt in 2014 to compete at a higher level. The next chapter of this deep rivalry starts Saturday night in Statesboro.

articles.summary: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc dominated practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix on Friday, clocking the fastest times in both sessions for the second weekend run...
articles.body:
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc dominated practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix on Friday, clocking the fastest times in both sessions for the second weekend running.

The Monegasque driver clocked a best lap in one minute and 17.827 seconds in the second practice session to outpace McLaren's world champion Lando Norris by 0.103 seconds with George Russell finishing third ahead of his Mercedes team-mate runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

Antonelli, 20, who was absent on Thursday to recover from a virus, can become the sport's youngest champion on Sunday, and Italy's first since 1963, if he finishes in the top nine.

He can also take the title if his two remaining rivals – Russell and Ferrari's seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton – fail to win.

Leclerc's success on Friday repeated his showing in Austin, Texas, at last weekend's United States Grand Prix.

Red Bull's four-time champion Max Verstappen, a record five-time winner in Mexico, was fifth ahead of team-mate Isack Hadjar after an early clash with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson which left him with damaged bodywork.

Lawson's team-mate Arvid Lindblad was seventh ahead of Alpine's Pierre Gasly, Lawson and Oscar Piastri in the second McLaren.

Seven-time champion Hamilton was down in 11th for Ferrari after suffering a power failure that ended his running midway through.

The session began with Gasly leading Alpine team-mate Franco Colapinto out ahead of Cadillac's local hero Sergio Perez, set for his 300th race start, the seventh driver to reach this landmark. He was promptly cautioned for a pit lane infringement.

After the inclusion of 10 rookie reserves in free practice one, all 22 full-timers were back with a wide range of tyres on show – Ferrari taking mediums, Verstappen softs and others hards on the low-grip track.

A red flag paused the action after 15 minutes to clear debris in the Foro Sol after Verstappen clashed with stable-mate Lawson and damaged his car's bargeboard.

The frustrated Dutchman's actions seemed excessively aggressive and required a Red Bull pit-stop for repairs. The incident was noted by the stewards and set for investigation afterwards.

Ferrari dominated the early stages with Leclerc on top before Norris, on softs, took command as McLaren bounced back shortly before Hamilton lost power and pulled up on the straight.

He had just switched to softs and completed one lap.

It was a setback for Hamilton who lost vital learning time on softs while Leclerc regained the initiative ahead of Norris, Russell and Antonelli before the field switched to heavier fuel loads and medium tyres.

articles.title: Bayern Munich’s Max Eberl talks Aaron Danks, Joshua Kimmich, and Der Klassiker
articles.summary: The FC Bayern exec is ready to face BVB.
articles.body:
With Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund level on points heading into Saturday's Der Klassiker , Max Eberl knows just how important the showdown could be in shaping the Bundesliga title race. The Bayern sporting director expressed his respect for Dortmund's development under Niko Kovač but made no secret of his ambitions for the match.

"We've got a lot of respect for Dortmund. We won in Dortmund last season, even though it was close. They were in good form as well last season and have continued that now. It's Der Klassiker . They always challenge and push us. We want to win and create a lead over BVB. We're currently equals in terms of the table," said Eberl (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

Eberl was also asked about Aaron Danks stepping into the spotlight on the touchline amid the unexpected circumstances surrounding Vincent Kompany. He praised the collective effort of the coaching staff and emphasized the importance of pulling together during a difficult period.

"Things have happened that can't be predicted. We have a coaching team that works together in an amazing way. We're really grateful to have Aaron and the team. It's not an easy situation. We're working hard to come through all this as a group. That's how things have to be in football," Eberl noted.

Finally, Eberl addressed Joshua Kimmich's personal situation following a family bereavement. While the midfielder has returned to individual training and could potentially feature against Dortmund, Eberl made it clear that Bayern will not put any pressure on him to return before he is ready.

"I've spoken with him. Life is different for him now. When something like that happens in the family, life changes for you. We'll give him all the support he needs. If Jo feels ready to get back involved, whether that could be tomorrow or not, he'll decide that with the coaching team. But we have to say that life is different for Jo now," said Eberl.

A massive game awaits Bayern Munich, but Eberl's comments also offered a reminder that there are things far more important than football. The club will give Kimmich all the time and support he needs.

articles.title: UIL reinstates Texas high school star QB Hayes Hackney ahead of regular-season finale
articles.summary: Argyle quarterback Hayes Hackney is eligible to return after the UIL overturned a residency ruling, clearing the star passer ahead of the playoffs.
articles.body:
Texas high school quarterback Hayes Hackney is eligible to return after the University Interscholastic League overturned a district committee's ruling that had sidelined him over residency concerns.

The UIL State Executive Committee voted 3-0 Thursday, Oct. 29, to restore Hackney's eligibility to play for Argyle High School, according to Texas HS Football .

The decision reverses an Oct. 20 ruling by the District 3-5A Division II Executive Committee, which voted 6-0 that Hackney, a transfer from Prosper Walnut Grove, did not meet residency requirements.

The dispute centered on whether Hackney's family lived within Argyle ISD boundaries while still owning a home in Prosper.

During Thursday's hearing, the state committee found sufficient evidence that the family lives in Argyle. School administrators had testified that they made multiple home visits to verify the family's residence.

State committee chairman Mike Motheral also questioned an earlier determination that Hackney had not transferred for athletic purposes. That issue was decided in May and was not part of Thursday's appeal.

Hackney has thrown for 2,574 yards and 32 touchdowns with just two interceptions this season. Argyle is 8-1 and ranked No. 3 in Class 5A Division II.

Argyle defeated Colleyville Heritage 45-35 last week with sophomore quarterback Cobe Wilson while Hackney was sidelined.

Hackney can return Friday when Argyle faces Nevada Community in its regular-season finale ahead of the playoffs.

An IHSA 6A first-round playoff game between No. 8 Sarah E. Goode STEM Academy and No. 9 Quincy Senior High School turned into a high-scoring affair as both offenses exploded for points early and often.

However, despite the electricity both of the offenses provided on the field, the game was moved from Goode High School's field to Chicago Englewood's field due to the field the game started on at 3 p.m. CT not having lights.

According to IHSA records , the 88 points are the second-most points in a single IHSA high school football playoff game since Peoria High School beat Decatur Eisenhower 96-40 on Nov. 4 in an IHSA playoff second-round game.

However, the combined 172 points is the most ever for a single game, besting the previous record of 166 set on Oct. 29, 2021, when Springfield High School defeated Rock Island High School 94-72.

articles.title: Russian return to ice hockey tournaments is ‘unwelcome,’ Carney says
articles.summary: A ruling from the Court of Arbitration for Sport orders ice hockey federations to allow Russia back into international competitions.
articles.body:
MONTREAL — A decision from the Court of Arbitration for Sport requiring Russian teams to be allowed back into international ice hockey tournaments is "unwelcome," Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney said Friday in an interview with POLITICO.

CAS ruled that the International Ice Hockey Federation can no longer bar Russia from participating in the coming World Junior Championship in Canada this December, as well as both the men's and women's world championships in May and November of next year, among other competitions.

On the sidelines of the EU-Canada summit in Montreal, Carney said he hadn't been aware of the decision, but noted, "It's unwelcome," adding, "I'll think about it."

Moscow has long used sports to project soft power abroad, and the ruling could make Canada an early test of Russia's return to international hockey, even as the war in Ukraine continues and other federations warn of security and political ramifications.

"The implications of today's decision by CAS are not immediately clear, and our organization is in contact with the IIHF to learn more," Hockey Canada said in a statement to POLITICO.

The IIHF, which runs the tournaments, also lamented the decision in a press release, but said it would honor the CAS ruling.

"The International Ice Hockey Federation expresses its disappointment with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport to allow the Russian Ice Hockey Federation in entering a Russian Team in all IIHF Championships with immediate effect," the statement reads.

The IIHF banned Russia from international hockey after the Kremlin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and rejected recent efforts from its federation to reintegrate national teams this summer , citing "ongoing safety, security and sporting integrity concerns."

CAS wrote in its ruling that those reasons were "not supported by sufficient evidence."

Moscow is already planning its return. In a statement Friday on Telegram , Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev, wrote that the "CAS ruling settles this issue, as it is final and cannot be appealed."

"Challenging work lies ahead as we work with the IIHF to implement the CAS ruling and secure Russian teams' return to competitions held under its auspices," he added.

But the Czech, German, Finnish and Swedish hockey federations blasted the ruling in statements Friday.

The German federation, which will host the next men's world tournament in May 2027, said the decision "would have significant security, political and economic consequences for [them] as hosts."

"I really hope the Danish team will pull out of the tournament," said Rasmus Jarlov , a former conservative Danish minister, on X. "It is not right to play sport games with Russia while Ukrainian athletes have to die at the front. I will be deeply disappointed if we participate."

articles.title: Oscar Piastri: McLaren handled Mexico altitude “better than I was expecting”
articles.summary: The McLaren driver believes he has more to come after a “messy” soft-tyre lap in FP2
articles.body:
McLaren driver Oscar Piastri walks away from FP2 in Mexico City's circuit with optimism as he confirms his car coped better with the high altitude than he expected it to. This comes despite the driver having a "pretty messy" qualifying simulation.

The Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez circuit sits more than 2,200 metres above sea level. The thin air leaves teams running with very little downforce and poor cooling, making it one of the most challenging weekends of the calendar.

Speaking after FP2, Piastri said the conditions had not been as tricky as he had feared.

"It was difficult for sure, but I don't think necessarily worse than what I was expecting, or if anything it was probably a little bit better than I was expecting. So yeah, everything felt OK. I think we seemed to be relatively competitive, to be honest."

The Australian admitted his soft-tyre lap failed to come together, but believed the papaya-coloured team's underlying pace is strong.

"My soft lap in FP2 was pretty messy, but I felt like the kind of overall pace seems to be there. So Ferrari looked very strong, which I guess you would kind of expect on a track like this, but I think we had a pretty good day."

Piastri said that cleaning up his mistakes should put him much higher up the order, but warned that beating Ferrari would be difficult.

"There was a couple of very big mistakes, so I'm optimistic that if I can tidy those up, I'll be a lot further up as well, which is a nice feeling to have. So I think to try and beat Ferrari tomorrow is going to be very tough, as it looks like. And it's very tight, I would say, through the whole field, so you're going to have to be on top of the game."

Asked how he had adapted his driving to the conditions, Piastri said the low grip was nothing new under this year's regulations.

"It's tough. It's just incredibly low grip. I think with this year's cars, honestly, it's a similar story in most places, so it doesn't feel that dramatic here. But it's always a challenge, not just for the car in terms of balance, but cooling the engines this year, it's always very tough."

Mercedes driver George Russell suggested on Thursday that Ferrari's smaller turbo could give it "quite an advantage" at altitude, with the 2026 rules having dropped the MGU-H that previously helped to eliminate turbo lag.

But Piastri doesn't agree that the turbo will be the deciding factor, adding that Ferrari didn't look especially fast in a straight line.

"They looked very quick today. I don't think the turbo is going to make as much of a difference as we thought. They, if anything, looked a bit slow on the straights, so let's wait and see tomorrow. Definitely in some circumstances it will help them, but I think in normal conditions it's not as big of a factor as we first thought."

articles.title: Barstool’s Joke about Raiders QB Goes Viral
articles.summary: A Barstool host called rookie QB Fernando Mendoza a perfect ex-boyfriend. The clip went viral fast, and Raiders fans are already ready for his start.
articles.body:
Some people just know how to tap into what fans feel without trying too hard. That is exactly what happened when a Barstool Sports personality compared rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza to a lost love. The comment aired during an episode of the "Big Boys Club" earlier this week and struck a nerve with everyone who watched Indiana win the national title. The clip has now racked up over 1.2 million views in just two days, proving that nostalgia sells better than any highlight reel.

Ella Grif did not hold back on her feelings about the Raiders' rookie. She told the show's hosts that she feels sad because the young quarterback reminds her of a perfect past relationship that is gone forever. "I'm sad because Fernando feels like the ex-boyfriend that was so perfect that you'll never get back. And you just look back on it, you compare everything to him," Grif said. That simple line explains why so many Hoosiers fans are already looking for a way to watch Mendoza play, even though he is now wearing a silver-and-black jersey.

The sadness Grif talked about comes from a specific moment in time that can never be repeated. Indiana fans know that winning the championship this year felt different because of the player at the helm. Even if the team wins every single game left on the schedule, the feeling will not match what they had with Mendoza. "And also, even if we went undefeated this year… Even if it was the same thing and we went to the Natty, it wouldn't feel the same… That makes me sad," she added. The emotional weight of that loss is real, and it makes the transition to the pros harder for the fans than the player.

This viral moment does more than just make people laugh; it changes the timeline for the Raiders. The team has lost four straight games after starting 3-0, and the pressure is mounting on Kirk Cousins to turn things around. With a 23-year-old talent waiting in the wings, the question is no longer if Mendoza will start, but when he will get the keys to the offense. According to the New York Post , the emotional impact he had on his former supporters will only increase Raiders fans' desire to see his return to the field soon.

While fans argue about the past, the present situation in Las Vegas demands a change. The Raiders need a spark, and the rookie from Indiana seems ready to provide it.

articles.title: Sherrock upsets Littler to claim £501,000 prize
articles.summary: Fallon Sherrock defeats reigning world champion Luke Littler in one leg of darts to win £501,000.
articles.body:
Fallon Sherrock defeated reigning world champion Luke Littler in one leg of darts on Friday to win £501,000.

Broadcast live globally on Netflix, Beat Luke Littler featured a host of amateur players taking on world number one Littler in a one-leg face-off at Manchester Central.

Players could not be members of the PDC Tour, meaning Sherrock, who became the first female player to beat a male opponent at the PDC World Championship on her way to the last 32 in December 2019, was allowed to compete.

After Littler had defeated 14 amateurs, some as young as 14, he was always going to have a tough task against 32-year-old Sherrock, a player who has won 21 times on the Women's PDC Series.

She had been closest to the bull to start first and hit a 180, only the third maximum of the night, before taking out double 20 to clinch the prize.

Sherrock, whose son Rory was among the crowd, said: "It's insane, I can't put it into words of what it means, especially having Rory here - it's his first time at anything and he has seen me win.

"It's a great moment and I will memorise this forever. Give me an opportunity and I will take it every time. I'm really proud of myself, I rise to the occasion."

Nineteen-year-old Littler, who has won the PDC World Championship in both the past two events, said: "Brilliant, that's what one person had to do - win the bull and go out in 15 [darts] and that's what she did, world class."

The packed crowd in Manchester was in boisterous mood with many fans in fancy dress, but this was darts with a difference.

There had been 25,000 applicants who had entered the competition.

The first stage saw players have to get down from 501 in 24 darts or less, with those successful then facing a three-person interview panel, including 16-time world champion Phil Taylor, PDC president Barry Hearn and darts television pundit Laura Turner.

Twenty players were due to play at the event. Sixteen were selected outright, while the eight most experienced players were paired off, with Netflix viewers voting on which one should be able to compete.

Sherrock was in the vote against Germany's Jarod Becker, but picked up 75% of the votes to get the chance to face Littler.

She had picked up £25,000 for reaching round three of the PDC World Championship at Alexandra Palace seven years ago after beating Ted Evetts and Mensur Suljovic before losing to Chris Dobey.

Her achievement saw her nicknamed 'The Queen of the Palace' and she was also awarded an MBE for her services to darts in 2023.

Sherrock's victory over Littler meant the event immediately ended, meaning the five remaining amateurs were unable to get their shot at the £501,000 prize.

Amateurs enjoy their moment in the spotlight

While Sherrock was celebrating, Ireland's 'Fierce' Pearse Mackle, a 21-year-old university student from County Cavan, was left wondering what could have been.

Mackle, who competes on PDC's Development Tour, was the eighth competitor and failed to hit a match-winning bullseye, instead finding the nine, and his life-changing moment came and went.

He was the only other player, apart from Sherrock, to cause Littler a fright.

For most of the night, Littler cruised through the competition as he went in search of the £501,000, which he had said he would donate to charity.

With former England footballer Gary Lineker hosting and with comedian Lee Mack and television presenter Richard Osman joining Turner as part of the punditry team, this was a night to bring darts to a new audience.

The first challenger was 16-year-old Kasey Smith from Manchester, but Littler showed he was in no mood to mess about, hitting treble 20s against her with his first two darts on his way to an easy win.

Some of Littler's opponents had never played a competitive game of darts, although everyone was keen to make the most of the experience.

With John McDonald, who retired as the main PDC master of ceremonies after the 2026 World Championship final, announcing the players before their elaborate walk-ons, this was a fun event, although most players came nowhere near beating Littler.

But there were still entertaining moments. Fourteen-year-old Jayden Walker, a year 10 pupil from Dorset, threw off a school blazer and tie to reveal his darts outfit and, as the third-highest ranked player, threatened to cause a huge shock.

But Littler raised his game when he needed to, hitting a maximum 180 followed by a 158 checkout, the highest of the night, to defeat his fellow teenager in only 12 darts.

Taylon Forrester, 18, described himself as a "binman who works with his dad" and he jumped out of a dumpster on his way to the oche.

Other entrants included Zac Spain, a jockey from Melbourne, Australia, Frenchman Theodore Wallich, who dubbed himself the 'Moustache Kid', 57-year-old Mark Pooke, another 14-year-old in Makinley Cooper-Johnson and Will Kemp, back playing after a heart attack earlier this year.

But Sherrock, whose participation in the competition had been questioned because of her past achievements in the sport, was the real winner, even if she had been described by Lineker as a "hairdresser from Milton Keynes".

With Littler on stage for more than two hours, he inevitably tired with his standard dropping and Sherrock was the one to take advantage, winning in a 15-dart leg in match number 15.

Hearn reappeared to present Sherrock with a huge cheque for her life-changing victory to end a surreal night of action.

articles.title: Maxi Arce y el ‘Gato’ Tello desafían los pronósticos y buscarán el milagro ante Tapia y Coello
articles.standfirst: En la final masculina del Kuwait Major
articles.summary: En la final masculina del Kuwait Major
articles.body: La primera semifinal enfrentaba a dos parejas poco habituales en estas rondas y con un objetivo común: alcanzar su primera final de Premier Padel juntos. Solo Tello sabía lo que era disputar una final de este nivel, después de haberlo conseguido en 2022. Los argentinos comenzaron mostrando su experiencia, presionando desde el resto y encontrando en Edu Alonso el principal objetivo de su estrategia para evitar que Goñi pudiera desplegar su potencial ofensivo. El primer break llegó en el tramo decisivo de la manga y permitió a Arce y Tello tomar ventaja por 6-4. La dinámica se mantuvo en el segundo set, cuando volvieron a romper el servicio de sus rivales y ganaron confianza para controlar el encuentro. Sin conceder oportunidades, terminaron cerrando el partido al resto, aprovechando un error de Alonso para sellar el 6-3 definitivo. Una victoria muy especial para ambos. Más de 1.500 días después, el ‘Gato’ Tello vuelve a una final, mientras que Maxi Arce reconocía tras el encuentro que se trata de la más importante de su carrera. Ahora, los argentinos tendrán ante sí el mayor desafío posible. En la segunda semifinal, disputada cerca de la medianoche en Kuwait, Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia no dieron opción a Tino Libaak y Leo Augsburger. Los Golden Boys saltaron a la pista con la máxima intensidad, conscientes del gran torneo que estaban firmando sus jóvenes rivales, pero dejaron claro desde el primer momento que no estaban dispuestos a conceder sorpresas. El dominio de los número uno fue absoluto de principio a fin. Tapia y Coello controlaron el ritmo, marcaron diferencias en todas las facetas del juego y no permitieron que Libaak y Augsburger encontraran argumentos para discutir su superioridad. El resultado, un contundente doble 6-2 que les permite alcanzar una nueva final. Ahora, el Kuwait Major tendrá una final con perspectivas muy distintas, por un lado, los indiscutibles dominadores del circuito, que buscarán ser número uno matemáticamente. Del otro, una pareja argentina que ha encontrado en Kuwait la oportunidad de protagonizar una de las grandes sorpresas de la temporada. Arce y Tello buscarán el milagro. articles.body:
Danhausen appropriately hosted a Halloween Eve edition of WWE SmackDown, live from Charleston, West Virginia, headlined by Sami Zayn defending his Undisputed WWE Championship against United States Champion Trick Williams.

What went down in the high-stakes main event? What did the very nice, very evil host have in store for the rest of the SmackDown brand?

Find out in this recap of the October 30 broadcast.

Announced in advance of Friday's show were:

Undisputed WWE Championship Match: Trick Williams vs. Sami Zayn (c)

WWE Women's Championship Match: Chelsea Green (c) vs. Nikki Bella

AAA Cruiserweight Championship Match: Rey Fenix (c) vs. Ricky Saints

Last Time in Action: Cody Rhodes defeated Baron Corbin via DQ (SmackDown, October 16)

After a Halloween-themed opening to the show featuring Danhausen, The American Nightmare took to the squared circle to kick things off.

Cody Rhodes apologized to Randy Orton's family for having to keep his promise to punt him in the face the next time he gets the chance.

He showed off the picture of his face after WrestleMania 42, where he nearly lost his eye and left Las Vegas a bloody mess, despite beating The Viper in their WWE Championship Match at that show.

A fired-up wrapped up his Crown Jewel hype promo, eight days before his Last Man Standing Match against his former mentor in short, sweet fashion.

This was a perfect opening promo. It was short and sweet promo that laid out the story and gave fans an idea of what to expect from Rhodes, who upped the ante by introducing Orton's family into the picture, much as his rival had done his.

This was the first time in weeks where the crowd seemed to be at least a little split on Rhodes. It will be interesting to see, if he is pushed over the edge, if that grows.

WWE Women's Championship Match: Chelsea Green vs. Nikki Bella

Last Time in Action: Chelsea Green defeated Roxanne Perez (SmackDown, October 23); Nikki Bella lost to Paige (SmackDown, October 16)

It was a case of Single White Female as Chelsea Green entered the arena dressed like her challenger, one final mind game before the bell rang.

Bella dominated entering the break but after, the champion mounted a comeback. The challenger stunted that with a big dropkick that netted her a two-count. Looking to match her mockery, Bella attempted a Broski Boot (ala Green's husband, Matt Cardona) but missed. Green responded with a Rough Ryder for a near-fall.

She survived the Fearless Lock and the Rack Attack, then caught Bella with a small package for the victory from nowhere.

After the match, Women's World Champion Liv Morgan, Green's opponent at Crown Jewel, appeared and called herself a real champion.

Tiffany Stratton appeared and teased a cash-in but was ambushed by Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez. Iyo Sky made the save, clearing the ring of the Judgment Day before checking on her fellow babyfaces.

The match was limited in time by the commercial break and everything that followed it was nearly a carbon copy of the same Judgment Day beatdown and Iyo Sky save that we have seen multiple times in recent weeks.

Stratton was badly nursing her left knee at one point during the beatdown.

Backstage, Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn cut a passionate promo on Roman Reigns. His contributions to the Crown Jewel rivalry have carried the program.

AAA Cruiserweight Championship Match: Rey Fenix vs. Ricky Saints

Last Time In Action: Rey Fenix defeated Jack Cartwheel, Kento, and Laredo Kid (AAA Heroes Inmortales 2026, October 24); Ricky Saints, Sami Zayn, and Johnny Gargano lost to Fenix, Penta, and Trick Williams (SmackDown, October 23)

Saints sought to end Fenix's run of successful title defenses Friday on SmackDown, going as far as to target the mask of his opponent while he controlled the pace of the bout.

Fenix fought back and rocked Absolute with a kick, but could not put him away. Saints answered with a Death Valley Driver but also netted just a two-count as chants of "this is awesome" rained down from the stands.

Late in the match, Saints looked for the Revolution but Fenix fought out. With the challenger on the top rope, Fenix tried a hurricanrana but was shoved to the mat. He rebounded quickly, delivered the Mexican Muscle Buster, and scored the win.

Fenix defeated Saints to retain the title

Backstage, Paige and Blake Monroe kicked off their rivalry with a verbal exchange that interrupted a Cathy Kelley interview with the latter.

This was the best Saints has looked outside of his series with Carmelo Hayes. SmackDown could benefit from more of his work.

Fenix finally looks comfortable and has momentum on his side. Like Chad Gable over on Raw, he has become the workhorse of the blue brand and can be counted on to deliver more weeks than not.

Last Time in Action: Tatum Paxley and Alexa Bliss lost to B-Fab and Michin (SmackDown, October 23); Jade Cargill lost to Jacy Jayne and Bliss (SmackDown, September 18)

Jade Cargill attempted to make Tatum Paxley an even sadder clown Friday night when the two squared off, the result of the former's cheap shot on the latter that cost her and Alexa Bliss the Women's Tag Team Championship.

A big knee by Cargill to Paxley's face stunned her, entering the commercial break as the Poison Ivy-costumed villain seized control.

During the break, Cargill dominated, trapping Paxley in a Boston Crab. The babyface fought back as the show returned to the air. She fired up, rocked her opponent with a pair of forearms and a step-up enzuigiri.

Late in the match, Michin and B-Fab made their presence felt at ringside, providing a distraction that allowed Cargill to recover and deliver a pumpkick for the win.

At least this repetitive, distraction-filled finale made sense within the context of the story being told. Michin and B-Fab benefited from Cargill inserting herself into last week's match and they repaid the favor here.

Why beat Paxley so much all of the sudden? She was garnering good reactions and had made a positive impact early in her run. Unless the goal is to put the title back on her and Bliss, this feels like an unnecessary cool down.

After months of backstage experiments, Danhausen made like Re-Animator and debuted his latest creation.

Gunther attacked him from behind, punishing the face-painted horror host before the minihausens made the save. The Ring General brutalized them, driving them through a pair of tables.

He put down Danhausen with a sleeper, but not before the babyface could issue a curse that was revealed to be The Demon, Finn Balor.

The crowd erupted for Balor, who unleashed a pair of kicks and no-sold a chop from Gunther before driving the former world champion through another table.

Balor ended the beatdown with a Coup de Grace from the top of a ladder to Gunther and through the announcer's table.

Backstage, Fraxiom interrupted an interview by Cathy Kelley with Damian Priest. Nathan Frazer talked his way into a match with The Archer of Infamy, to which Priest warned that if he brutalized Truth and he likes him, imagine what he will do to either of them.

Gunther, for the first time in his career, displayed a genuine look of fear as The Demon entered the ring and that did more to put over this incarnation of the former Universal Champion than any win ever could.

Did this feud necessarily warrant The Demon? Not really, but if there is any way to convince fans that Balor stands a chance against the Career Killer, having him break out his mostly unbeatable alter-ego is a great way to do it. That the segment was great and Gunther sold the moment perfectly only helped.

Undisputed WWE Championship Match: Trick Williams vs. Sami Zayn

Last Time In Action: Trick Williams, Penta, and Rey Fenix defeated Sami Zayn, Johnny Gargano, and Ricky Saints (SmackDown, October 23) ; Zayn defeated Je'Von Evans (Raw, October 26)

Like Michael Myers every Halloween, the rivalry between Sami Zayn and Trick Williams was resurrected for the main event of Friday's broadcast.

Zayn controlled during the commercial break, looking to prove his assertions correct that Williams was not ready to be the top guy on Friday nights; that he does not have the required "it" to be the WWE champ.

Williams fought back, stomping Zayn in the corner. The heel hung him up on the ropes to thwart his comeback, but the United States Champion rocked him with a jumping knee.

Zayn recovered and sought a Helluva Kick, but Williams cut him off. Johnny Gargano tried to interfere, but Lil Yachty countered him. Candice LeRae threw the WWE title to Zayn, but Williams delivered the Book End, only for Gargano to pull referee Charles Robinson to the floor and draw a disqualification.

Or so it appeared. SmackDown general manager Nick Aldis appeared and made the match No Disqualification, but not before escorting the outside parties out of the arena.

Zayn attacked Williams with a kendo stick emerging from the break, only for the challenger to deliver a neck breaker. He rocked Zayn with a big kick but could not keep him down for the win and the title.

The champion recovered and delivered a Blue Thunder Bomb on a pile of steel chairs, but still only netted a two-count. Williams recovered and delivered a Trick Shot, but Zayn survived.

The so-called Last Real Good Guy used Robinson as a shield, delivered a low blow, and blasted his opponent with a championship shot to the face for the win.

The match was good enough without the need for the GM restart and No DQ gimmick. Considering Zayn cheated to win anyway, why not just continue the story of him manipulating Gargano and LeRae into helping him?

Williams will be just fine, but the United States Championship definitely takes a blow with the loss here. Based on Damian Priest's disgust over his championship opportunity, could a feud between him and Trick be up next?

Finn Balor's return as The Demon was amazing and easily the single most memorable moment of this show. With that said, it was enhanced significantly by Gunther's facial expressions and sell job. He displayed fear and made the fans at home recognize the dire situation that he found himself in.

Has his recent usage been great? No, but Gunther at his best is special.

There was some fun stuff here, including the main event and the aforementioned notable segment. Cody Rhodes delivered a pinpoint promo that did not overstay its welcome, and Fenix vs. Ricky Starks had the best in-ring performances of the week.

Still, it felt very much like a placeholder show ahead of next week's go-home edition before Crown Jewel, and the two women's segments felt oddly familiar, at least if you have been paying attention in recent weeks, and both of those knocks prevent land it squarely in "B" territory.

articles.title: NHL's reigning MVP Nikita Kucherov reportedly asks Lightning for trade in stunning move
articles.summary: Nikita Kucherov has reportedly asked the Tampa Bay Lightning to trade him and told teammates he will not re-sign after this season.
articles.body: According to multiple reports, Tampa Bay Lightning star Nikita Kucherov — the reigning Hart Memorial Trophy-winner as the NHL's MVP — has informed the team that he will not re-sign and would like a trade. Go ahead and pick your jaw up off the floor after that one. Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that Kucherov had informed the team and his teammates of his plans to sign elsewhere when his 8-year, $76 million deal ends after this season. The prevailing thought was that Kucherov would almost certainly re-sign with the Lightning. He's been their centerpiece through three runs to the Stanley Cup Final and the team is still playing well.
